newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ sees cattle-driven farming recovery in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: NZ sees cattle-driven farming recovery in 1997/98.

text.p: New Zealand's Ministry of Agriculture and Food forecast on Tuesday that the value of agricultural production would increase by around 1.5 percent in the year to March 1988, largely on expected increases in dairy and beef production and small rises in wool, sheepmeat and pipfruit prices.
However, MAF predicted volumes of wool, sheepmeat, kiwifruit and pipfruit would all fall.
It estimated that earnings in the year to March 1997 fell by 3.0 percent on an annual basis, mainly due to falls in production and prices of cattle and wool.

In comments in its "Situation and Outlook for New Zealand Agriculture" report, MAF said that after another year of mixed fortunes in 1996/97 there was now some recovery in sheepmeat and beef markets, although demand for wool has fallen further.
"Dairy is performing well, although markets have been less favourable...(and) confidence in deer remains high," the ministry added.

Among the major horticultural commodities, apples and kiwifruit faced tough competition, it noted, though export prices gave reasonable returns to those orchards not affected by hail during the last season.
In terms of the performance seen during the current year, MAF said revenue for the average beef and sheep farm were set to increase slightly in 1996/7, as were average dairy revenues.

It forecast pipfruit orchard revenues for the year ending September 1997 would increase by 2.0 percent for orchards not affected by hailstorms, while kiwifruit orchards revenues rose by 5.0 percent in the year to the end of March.
